themes_detail.label: Street obstructions surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints spiked to 43 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 19.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 119% jump (z-score: 8.02)—suggesting a sudden and acute problem with sidewalks, curbs, or street access being blocked across CD 412.
evidence: 43 obstruction complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (119% spike)
Z-score of 8.02 indicates statistically significant deviation
Aligns with longstanding community board request to repair sidewalks, curbs, and pedestrian ramps
reporting_angles: What specific obstructions are blocking streets—illegally parked cars, vendor stalls, construction debris, fallen branches?
Are obstructions concentrated in one neighborhood area or scattered across Jamaica/Hollis/St. Albans?

themes_detail.label: Tree overgrowth blocking streets and sidewalks
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints reached 8 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.9 per week—a 178% increase (z-score: 4.87)—while dead/dying tree complaints hit 8 LAST WEEK versus 2.1 baseline, suggesting accelerating vegetation hazards that may be contributing to the obstruction spike.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branches: 8 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average (178% spike, z-score: 4.87)
Dead/dying trees: 8 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (276% spike, z-score: 5.04)
Aligns with longstanding CB requests for park maintenance and safety (DPR)
reporting_angles: Are DPR tree trimming schedules keeping pace with growth in the district, or are budgets/staffing insufficient?
Which parks or corridors are most affected—Jamaica Center, St. Albans Park, Hollis Park, or residential blocks?

themes_detail.label: Street sweeping and curb maintenance failures
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints surged to 10 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 789% spike (z-score: 8.43)—while curb condition complaints hit 8 LAST WEEK versus 1.6 baseline (392% spike), indicating sanitation service gaps and physical street deterioration.
evidence: Street sweeping complaints: 10 LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (789% spike, z-score: 8.43)
Curb condition complaints: 8 LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (392% spike, z-score: 7.44)
Longstanding CB request for more on-street trash cans and recycling containers (DSNY) suggests chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Has DSNY reduced sweeping frequency or reallocated crews away from CD 412?
Are sidewalk/curb condition issues creating public health hazards or barriers for elderly/disabled residents?

themes_detail.label: Park rules enforcement spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violation complaints spiked to 5 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3,900% increase (z-score: 14.74, highest severity alert)—suggesting either a sudden change in park behavior or a surge in enforcement/reporting.
evidence: Park rules violation complaints: 5 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3,900% spike, z-score: 14.74)
Highest z-score of all spikes in the dataset—most statistically anomalous signal
Aligns with CB requests for park maintenance and safety (DPR)
reporting_angles: What specific violations spiked—unlicensed vendors, after-hours activity, dangerous behavior, or rule changes?
Which parks—Jamaica Center Park, St. Albans Park, Hollis Park—are seeing violations?

themes_detail.label: Wood debris accumulation in district
themes_detail.summary: Wood pile remaining complaints jumped to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—indicating possible storm debris cleanup failures or contractor/construction site violations.
evidence: Wood pile remaining complaints: 3 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
May be related to recent weather events, tree removal operations, or construction sites
No recent news mentions or CB discussions provide context
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm, tree removal program, or major construction project triggering debris accumulation?
Is DSNY responsibly removing debris, or are contractors/private parties abandoning materials?
